project.name: Jesus Christ Saves Token
project.current_stage: Public static application under active top-down modernization.
project.description_short: A Christ-centered, non-custodial XRP Ledger application for prayer, testimony, Scripture, public verification, sacred media, and responsible community tools.
project.description_long: Jesus Christ Saves Token combines a faith-centered website, user-controlled Xaman authorization, XRP Ledger data, prayer and testimony NFTs, public verification, Scripture and sacred-media experiences, and a developing social interface. The present deployment is primarily static and client-side. The long-term direction is JCS Fellowship, a privacy-conscious Christian social platform designed around prayer, encouragement, service, finite use, and human dignity rather than speculative status or attention extraction.
project.mission: Use transparent technology as a vessel for prayer, testimony, Scripture, service, and Christian community while keeping Jesus Christ, faith, human dignity, and user-controlled wallets above the token or application.
project.religious_boundary: JCS technology, tokens, NFTs, websites, applications, and communities do not replace Jesus Christ, Scripture, prayer, fellowship, church, pastoral care, professional assistance, emergency services, or personal responsibility.

xrpl.verification_rule: Verify the complete issuer account and currency code. A ticker, logo, social post, or similarly named asset is not sufficient identification.

identity_limits: A public wallet address does not establish a person's legal identity.
A Web DID does not prove every off-ledger claim.
A wallet signature proves account control for that event, not the truth of a prayer, testimony, biography, or ownership claim.
References to Ripple, Xaman, GitHub, explorers, exchanges, or infrastructure providers do not imply endorsement, partnership, custody, or shared control.

current_application.hosting: GitHub Pages with the jesuschristsavestoken.com custom domain
current_application.delivery_model: Primarily static HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with client-side wallet and public-data interactions.
capabilities: Public JCS faith and project portal
Public XRP Ledger and DEX information
On-ledger testimony, reply, and Amen-reaction functions where implemented
Public identity, security, legal, and machine-readable metadata
Local browser processing and storage where implemented
limitations: The current static deployment is not a complete centralized or federated social network.
There is no universal JCS profile database, private-message service, real-time moderation system, or guaranteed content-delivery service.
Third-party endpoints, wallet services, media providers, market interfaces, and public XRPL servers may be delayed, unavailable, rate-limited, or changed.
A page existing in the repository does not prove every external integration is currently operational.

concepts.name: Scripture Path

ethical_product_rules.core_principle: Spiritual access, safety, and human dignity must not depend on wealth or token ownership.
prohibited_design_patterns: paid priority for crisis or pastoral needs
gambling or pay-to-win Prayer Garden mechanics
publishing private personal data by default
ethical_product_rules.gating_status: No universal future gating model is established by this manifest. Any later gate must be disclosed and must respect the prohibited-design rules.

current.browser_storage: Local browser storage may be used by individual pages where disclosed.
third_party_services: public XRPL servers or project proxies

moderation queues, blocking, reporting, and appeals
rate limiting, abuse prevention, and anti-spam
backups, administrative audit logs, and account recovery
legal, privacy, child-safety, accessibility, and security review
architecture.architecture_rule: Secrets and privileged logic must not be placed in the public GitHub Pages frontend.

wallet_flow: The page reads public data or prepares a proposed transaction.
The user opens Xaman and reviews the request.
The user approves or rejects the transaction.
The application checks a validated XRPL result when final confirmation is required.
wallet_and_ledger_safety.public_ledger_warning: XRPL accounts, transactions, balances, trust lines, offers, AMMs, NFTs, token IDs, URIs, memos, and related records may be publicly observable indefinitely.
wallet_and_ledger_safety.transaction_finality_rule: A wallet approval or submitted payload is not necessarily final. When completion matters, use a validated ledger result and inspect the result and metadata.
wallet_and_ledger_safety.nft_evidence_rule: An NFT or validated transaction can document a technical ledger event. It does not automatically prove real-world identity, truth, authorship, legal ownership, pastoral authority, institutional acceptance, or entitlement to a response.

evidence_model.observed: Returned directly by a validated XRPL or identified external source.
evidence_model.derived: Calculated from observed values using a disclosed method.
evidence_model.unknown_or_unavailable: Not established by the retrieved evidence and must not be silently converted to zero, safe, fraudulent, or complete.

data_and_metrics.freshness_policy: Metrics are snapshots. Record the validated-ledger reference and retrieval time when available. Failures must be shown as unavailable or partial evidence.

methods.name: JCS/XRP funded order-book reference
methods.method: Use funded executable amounts when returned, preserve book-side orientation, convert XRP drops correctly, and distinguish an empty book from a failed query.
limitations: Displayed offers can change before execution.
Funded depth is not a guarantee of fill.
Maker accounts do not establish beneficial ownership.

methods.name: JCS/XRP AMM reference
methods.method: Identify XRP and JCS reserves, calculate a reserve-ratio reference, disclose price-impact assumptions, and convert the raw trading fee from units of 1/100,000.
limitations: Reserve ratio is not a guaranteed execution price.
Liquidity, fees, and price impact can change before validation.

methods.name: Issuer obligations
methods.method: Use reported obligations when the selected public service supports the request.
methods.fallback: A bounded, paginated issuer account_lines scan may provide an observed sample, but must be labeled as a fallback rather than an authoritative total.

methods.name: Observed trust-line and holder sample
methods.method: Follow returned pagination markers within a disclosed cap and report the number of lines, pages, positive balances, and whether the scan was truncated.
limitations: Wallet addresses are not unique people.
One party can control multiple accounts.

methods.name: External XRP/USD reference
methods.method: Use only as an external reference and identify the provider on the page using it.
limitations: External prices may be delayed, unavailable, jurisdiction-specific, or inconsistent with executable XRPL liquidity.

methods.name: Indicative JCS reference in USD
methods.method: Multiply a disclosed JCS/XRP reference by an identified XRP/USD reference.
limitations: This is not a formal valuation, appraisal, reserve attestation, guaranteed realizable value, or promise of liquidity.

methods.name: Indicative network value
methods.method: When displayed, multiply a disclosed reference price by a disclosed obligations or supply figure.
limitations: Thin liquidity can make a multiplication-based figure economically misleading.
The figure is not a securities valuation or evidence of available exit liquidity.

principles: Collect or expose only the minimum information necessary for a feature.
Do not place sensitive personal information in public NFT metadata or XRPL memos.
A hidden wallet address in the interface remains public if it appears on-ledger.
Local browser storage is device- and profile-dependent and can be cleared, copied, or compromised.
Third-party media, wallet, map, market, and infrastructure providers apply their own privacy practices.
sensitive_content_not_for_public_ledger: precise location when disclosure could create danger
information identifying persecuted or vulnerable people

verification_workflow: Verify the canonical domain and Web DID.
Verify the exact JCS issuer and currency code.
Use validated XRPL data for ledger claims.
Inspect the page-specific implementation before claiming a function is operational.
Separate observed evidence, derived calculations, and unknown information.
Compare independent explorers only as secondary sources.
State data freshness, retrieval limits, and unavailable evidence.
safe_interaction_rules: Never ask for a seed phrase, private key, recovery words, wallet passcode, or remote-access credentials.
Direct users to review every transaction in Xaman.
Do not claim finality without a validated result when finality matters.
Do not encourage sensitive personal information in public prayer, testimony, NFT metadata, or XRPL memos.
Do not infer real-world identity from a public wallet.
Do not rank spiritual worth by token holdings, transaction volume, NFT count, or market value.
content_status_rules: Use current_application for deployed or legacy-current resources.
Use planned_application only as roadmap context.
Do not merge planned features into current functionality.
Do not describe a compatibility route as a separate full application.
Do not treat independent services as official JCS infrastructure.
citation_guidance: For ledger claims, cite the relevant validated XRPL record.
For project identity, cite the canonical domain, Web DID, XRP Ledger TOML, or repository.
For current features, cite the specific page implementing the feature.
For policies and limitations, cite Privacy, Terms, Security, LICENSE, README, or this manifest.
Do not quote prayer or testimony as verified factual evidence beyond its public existence.
